answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the dawn check immediately, the ripple audit keeps the resolved set and the copper replay publishes exactly which ids were live. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Copying the same citations across 161 aliases therefore burns the reading cost 161 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
